1. (Currently amended) An air braking unit for use in an air braking system, the air braking unit being arranged to be positioned, in use, at a vehicle wheel, and comprising: an inlet for receiving, in use, compressed air from a central source; at least one first valve arranged to selectively allow compressed air from the inlet to enter a wheel brake chamber in use; at least one second valve arranged to selectively allow air from the brake chamber to be released via an outlet to the atmosphere in use; and control means for controlling the first and second valves to operate to selectively control the air pressure in the brake chamber in use, wherein the control means further includes software programmed to adapt the control of the first and second valves based on variations in vehicle speed. 

2. (Currently amended) The air braking unit of claim 1, further comprising plural first valves and/or plural second valves, wherein the plural valves may comprise larger valves arranged to allow large volumes of air to pass therethrough and smaller valves arranged to allow passage of smaller volumes of air therethrough.

3. (Currently amended) The air braking unit of claim 2, wherein the one or more smaller valves are arranged to operate at high speed, providing rapid response to changes in brake pressure demands.

4. (Currently amended) The air braking unit of claim 3, wherein one or more of the valves are driven by binary actuators, specifically configured to enhance operational efficiency with respect to air pressure control.

5. (Currently amended) An air braking unit according to any preceding claim, wherein the control means is arranged to receive control signals from a wheel speed sensor and an air pressure sensor for determining the pressure in the brake chamber and adjust the control signals dynamically based on those measurements. 

6. (Currently amended) An air braking unit according to any preceding claim, wherein the control means is arranged to receive data from a vehicle speed sensor, and reference data indicative of an optimum braking force for varying vehicle and wheel speeds and to control braking force based thereon, utilizing a feedback loop for continuous adjustment.

7. (Currently amended) An air braking unit according to claim 6, wherein the control means is arranged to determine, from the sensors, and stored reference data, an optimum speed for each wheel and to control the braking force on each wheel in accordance with the calculated optimum speed, incorporating real-time adjustments based on feedback from the vehicle performance.

8. (Currently amended) An air braking system comprising one or more units according to any preceding claim; a pump for generating compressed air; and a central compressed air storage tank, wherein the system further includes a pressure relief mechanism to ensure safety during operation.
